raw_response:
My family has farmed this land for generations. My husband and I have about 6 mu, the same fields my in-laws worked. I don't read much, but I know this land. Everyone around me grows winter wheat then summer maize — that's what we do here. I've never tried anything different. The soil is flat, the well is close, and the grain station buys both crops. There's no reason to change.

For wheat, I'll ask my neighbor which seeds he bought last year — he had a good harvest. Probably something from the county seed shop, one of those improved varieties they've been pushing. Not the old seeds, those yield less. For maize I always buy the hybrid packets from the market, same as everyone else.

Fertilizer — I put down more than I probably need, but I'd rather not lose the crop. My mother-in-law always said the land needs to eat too. I'll do a base application before wheat planting and topdress at jointing. For maize I'll apply at planting and again when it's knee-high.

Irrigation: wheat needs water when it's cold (冬水), at jointing, and at heading. Maize mostly catches summer rain but I'll pump once if it gets dry.

I'll hire a rotary tiller before wheat goes in. For maize I just plant straight into the stubble after wheat harvest — saves money and time.
